questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to **candid**.
questions.explanation: Candid means honest and direct in speech.

questions.question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to **expand**.
questions.explanation: To expand is to become larger; to contract is to become smaller.

questions.question: One word for "a person who speaks several languages":
questions.explanation: A polyglot knows many languages. An orator is a public speaker.

questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to **diligent**.
questions.explanation: Diligent means careful and persistent in work.

questions.question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to **transparent**.
questions.explanation: Transparent lets light through; opaque does not.

questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to **defer**.
questions.explanation: To defer is to put off to a later time.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The news ___ spread quickly through the campus.
questions.explanation: "News" is uncountable and singular: has spread.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: I look forward to ___ you next week.
questions.explanation: In "look forward to", "to" is a preposition, so the verb takes -ing.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: He is good ___ mathematics.
questions.explanation: The usual phrase is "good at" a subject or skill.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: She ___ her lunch when the power went off.
questions.explanation: A past action in progress that was interrupted needs the past continuous.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Hardly had he reached the station ___ the train left.
questions.explanation: "Hardly ... when" is the correct pair. "Than" goes with "no sooner".

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The teacher, along with the students, ___ going on a trip.
questions.explanation: "Along with" does not make the subject plural; the verb agrees with "teacher".

questions.question: Fill in the blank: He is the ___ of the two brothers.
questions.explanation: Two things are compared, so the comparative "taller" is used.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Neither the manager nor the clerks ___ present.
questions.explanation: With "neither ... nor" the verb agrees with the nearer subject, "clerks" (plural).

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: Separate has "par" in the middle: sep-a-rate.

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: Government comes from govern + ment; keep the n.

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: Embarrass has double r and double s.

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: Recommend: one c, double m.

questions.question: Change to the passive voice: Someone has stolen my bag.
questions.explanation: Present perfect active becomes "has/have been + past participle".

questions.question: Change to the passive voice: Open the window.
questions.explanation: An imperative becomes "Let + object + be + past participle".

questions.question: Change to the active voice: The tickets will be booked by Rahul.
options: Rahul will be booking the tickets.
questions.explanation: The future tense is kept: will book.

questions.question: Change to indirect speech: She said, "I will call you tomorrow."
options: She said that she will call you tomorrow.
She said that she would call me the next day.
She said that I would call her the next day.
She said that she would call you tomorrow.
questions.explanation: "Will" becomes "would", "you" becomes "me", and "tomorrow" becomes "the next day".

questions.question: Change to indirect speech: The officer said to him, "Leave the room."
options: The officer said him to leave the room.
The officer ordered that he leaves the room.
The officer asked that leave the room.
The officer ordered him to leave the room.
questions.explanation: A command is reported with "ordered/told + object + to + verb".

questions.question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: **to let the cat out of the bag**.
options: to make a mistake in a bag
questions.explanation: It means to give away a secret by accident.

questions.question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: **to cry over spilt milk**.
options: to regret something that cannot be undone
questions.explanation: It means to waste time grieving over a past mistake.

questions.question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: **to hit the sack**.
questions.explanation: "Sack" here means bed.

questions.question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: **a piece of cake**.
questions.explanation: It describes a task that is effortless.

questions.question: A memorandum (memo) is mainly used for:
questions.explanation: A memo is a brief internal message.

questions.question: The subject line of a letter:
options: states briefly what the letter is about
questions.explanation: It lets the reader see the purpose at a glance.

questions.question: "Yours faithfully" is used when:
options: the letter begins with "Dear Mr Rao"
there is no salutation at all
questions.explanation: Use "faithfully" with a general salutation and "sincerely" with a named person.

questions.question: In office writing, "ASAP" stands for:
questions.explanation: ASAP is a common abbreviation for as soon as possible.

questions.passage:
**Read the passage and answer the next 3 questions.**
Cloud storage lets users keep files on remote servers instead of on their own devices. The files can be opened from any place with an internet connection, and several people can work on the same document together. However, the user depends on the service provider for security and availability. If the provider's servers fail, or if the user forgets the account password, access to the files may be lost. For this reason, important files are best kept in more than one place.
questions.question: What is a benefit of cloud storage, according to the passage?
options: Files can be opened from any place with an internet connection.
questions.explanation: The second sentence says files can be opened from any place with an internet connection.

questions.passage:
**Read the passage and answer the next 2 questions.**
The campus has a rule that bicycles must be parked only in marked stands. Vehicles found elsewhere are removed by the security staff, and a fine of Rs. 100 is charged to get them back. Students are advised to lock their cycles even inside the stands.
questions.question: What happens to a cycle parked outside the marked stands?
options: It is locked by the owner.
It is given to a student.
It is removed and a fine is charged.
questions.explanation: Security staff remove it and a fine of Rs. 100 is charged to get it back.

questions.question:
Arrange the sentences in the correct order.

P. Therefore, the update was installed on a Sunday night.
Q. The old software had a serious security flaw.
R. Fixing it could not be delayed.
S. No users were working at that time.
questions.explanation: Flaw (Q), urgency (R), so the update (P), reason it was safe (S).

questions.question:
Arrange the sentences in the correct order.

P. She prepared a list of questions.
Q. Asha had an interview the next morning.
R. She also practised answering them aloud.
S. Then she went to bed early.
questions.explanation: "Them" in R refers to the questions in P, so P comes before R.

questions.question:
Arrange the sentences in the correct order.

P. Many of them stayed on and settled nearby.
Q. Hundreds of workers came to build the dam.
R. The work went on for ten years.
S. By the end, a small market town had grown around the site.
questions.explanation: Workers arrive (Q), work continues (R), many stay (P), town grows (S).

questions.question:
Arrange the sentences in the correct order.

P. Hence, users who ignore updates stay exposed.
Q. New security flaws are found in software every month.
R. Attackers quickly learn to use them.
S. Software makers therefore release updates to close these gaps.
questions.explanation: Flaws (Q), attackers (R), updates as the answer (S), conclusion "Hence" (P).
